Action: Search your email and messages for the dentist's November confirmations for you and Leo, and tell you what I find (or draft a request to the office if nothing is there).

The two numbers to pin down first are what the 10% is in actual dollars after tax, and what the commute costs him: 45 minutes on the subway versus a 10 minute bike ride is about 70 minutes back every working day. If the jobs are otherwise similar I'd lean toward the short commute, but he should settle it on caseload, mentorship and room to grow first, and use pay and commute as the tiebreaker. A good question for you to put to him: 'If they paid the same, which one would you pick?'
Action: Draft a short text you can send Marcus with those questions.

Yes, I can do that. I'll use the scan date from each PDF's metadata and fall back to the file's modified date if there isn't one, naming them YYYY-MM-DD_Scan.pdf and adding a number when two share a date. I'll show you the full list of old and new names first so nothing gets renamed by surprise.

EFT is the broad term for electronic funds transfers that clear in batches, like direct deposits and pre-authorized debits: cheap, usually a few business days, and they can be returned. A wire is a one-off, same-day payment that is effectively final and costs much more. So for merchant payouts EFT is the normal rail, and a wire is for when you need speed and certainty on a large amount.
Action: Draft a one-line definition of each for you to drop into the deck so sales stops mixing them up.

Yes, I'll build the failed payout breakdown by receiving bank for the last 30 days, with failure reason alongside if the data has it, ready for Wednesday's roadmap prep. One thing to handle in the numbers: my notes say bank-side failures are retried automatically (that note is five weeks old), so I'll separate payouts that failed and later succeeded on retry from those that ended failed.
Action: Pull the last 30 days of failed payouts grouped by receiving bank and send you the table, noting which data source I used.

Ha, that's a very Leo question, and a long day on top of it would wipe anyone out. At least one dinosaur thing is handled: the T-Rex costume arrives Tue 27 Jan.
Action: Nothing for tonight; I'll leave the rest of the to-do list alone.

Night, Riya. Congrats again on the launch.
Action: None tonight; the wins record note is saved for your review.

You made it, and it was a lot of threads in one week: the bio, the meetup details and Leo's swim registration all landed. Nothing urgent from my side for tonight. The next meetup deadline is the talk title, due by 18 Sep.
Action: None tonight; I'll keep the weekend light and put the talk title deadline on next week's list.

Yes to pancakes at Hannah's, Sunday at 9 with the kids. I'll text her back and put it on the family calendar, and check it doesn't collide with anything else that morning.

It used to be late January, and yes, it moved because the NFL season got longer. The 2002 game slipped into February after the 9/11 postponement, and the move to a 17-game regular season in 2021 keeps it in the second week of February. Sunday is just TV: it's the biggest audience night of the week.

This week I'd focus on the subjunctive and the noun-gender exceptions you keep missing (el problema, el mapa, el tema, la mano), plus Carlos's emailed homework, with the DELE B2 on Sat 21 Nov in the background. Your lesson with Carlos is Thursday at 19:30, so I'd block two short study sessions earlier in the week and a 20-minute warm-up before class on Thursday. I'll check those slots against your calendar first.
Action: Check your calendar, block the two study sessions and the Thursday pre-class warm-up, and pull Carlos's latest homework email into your Spanish notes.

I don't have a rink status for Withrow yet, and conditions can change day to day, so I'll check rather than guess. I'll look at the City's rink listing and Saturday afternoon's forecast.

Action: Put those in a short note you can forward to Diego.

On it. The sheet will have three sections: ser vs estar (estar for emotions and where things are, ser for what something is), por vs para, and the future subjunctive after cuando, starting from your own example, 'cuando llego a casa te llamo' becoming 'cuando llegue a casa te llamo'. Each section gets about ten short fill-in-the-blank items, with an answer key at the bottom.
Action: Write the drill sheet and save it to your notes so it's ready before your next lesson.

A heat warning means two or more days of very high heat are expected; an extended heat warning means the heat is forecast to last three or more days. In southern Ontario the rough trigger is daytime highs around 31 and overnight lows around 20, or a humidex near 40. The precautions are the same, but with an extended one plan for several hot nights in a row.
Action: None, though I can silence the alerts for tonight if the buzzing is too much.
